items.title: I Got Tired of Remembering Ports for 30 Docker Apps in My Homelab. Here's How I Fixed it
items.summary: My homelab runs on 5 machines with around 30 Docker containers. For a long time, the way I reached them was a bookmarks folder full of entries like http://100.101.12.4:8096. Tailscale took care of getting me into my network from anywhere, but once I was in, I was back to remembering which box ran what on which port. The usual fixes each have a catch. A reverse proxy with your own domain works, but it's one more thing to maintain, and every new app means touching two config files instead of one. Giving each container its own Tailscale sidecar gets you nice names, but it also turns the Machines page into a list of containers, each with its own auth key and state volume.

items.title: Linux 7.3 Will More Than Likely Be This Year's LTS Kernel
items.summary: While the Linux 7.4 kernel will be released in the 2026 calendar year in the last week or two of December if the schedule holds, it turns out Linux 7.3 is likely to be this year's Long Term Support kernel version. Typically the Linux LTS kernel for a given year is the last major version shipped that calendar year. Even if Linux 7.4 ships with a one week delay it will be out on 27 December as opposed to a 20 December ideal target date. So while a Linux 7.4 release will most likely be here in 2026, Greg Kroah-Hartman as the stable/LTS maintainer is leaning towards Linux 7.3 for the LTS version.

Conductor confirmed it’s joining Meta in a post on its website. Terms were not disclosed. The company’s software lets a developer run several coding agents at once, each in an isolated copy of the codebase, and then…

items.title: China Unveils Their Plan for a Crewed Moon Landing
items.summary: Yesterday, on November 3rd, the deputy chief designer of China's crewed space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program (Wang Xiang) unveiled an official statement detailing its [plans for a crewed mission to the Moon](https://english.spacechina.com/n17212/c4744561/content.html).

items.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
items.summary: In an emergency, a human might someday ask a robotic assistant to fetch a wall-mounted defibrillator located down the hall. But if the robot has incorrectly labeled the defibrillator as a fire extinguisher in its stored memory, it may not know where to find the life-saving device. This robotic assistant could benefit from a new memory system created by MIT researchers. The system identifies entries in a robot’s memory that might be wrong and corrects the descriptions of mislabeled objects.

items.title: 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live
items.summary: Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency 's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT).

items.title: After Texas' blue wave, what happens to Elon Musk and SpaceX?
items.summary: Following his public disputes with California authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic, Elon Musk personally moved to Texas, outside of Austin, in 2020. Over the next six years, he doubled down on the Lone Star State. In 2021, Musk increasingly focused the Starship program in South Texas, urging SpaceX employees to move there and work on the company's future. In March of that year, he began using the name Starbase to describe the production and launch facilities near the Rio Grande River. In 2023, he built a massive factory east of Austin to manufacture customer terminals and other electronics for the Starlink program.

items.title: Democrat Amish Shah leads Republican Jay Feely in Arizona’s 1st Congressional District
items.summary: Democrat Amish Shah leads Republican Jay Feely in the race for Arizona’s 1st Congressional District. Decision Desk HQ projected Shah as the winner Wednesday evening. The Associated Press has not called the race. As of Wednesday evening, the results showed Shah ahead 52.5% to 45.4%, with a margin of 22,494 votes and 206 of 210 precincts reporting. The difference of 7 percentage points was smaller than the 11.6-point gap after Tuesday’s first wave of results. The open northeast Valley seat was one of House Democrats’ top targets this year.

items.title: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reenters over Western Indonesia
items.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory plummeted back into Earth’s atmosphere Wednesday over western Indonesia, ending nearly 22 years in orbit for the gamma-ray burst hunter after a failed attempt to rescue it. Swift re-entered at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 UTC) near 3 degrees north latitude and 99 degrees east longitude, over Indonesia’s North Sumatra region, according to U.S. Space Force tracking data later confirmed by NASA. “NASA expected most of the spacecraft to burn up as it traveled through the atmosphere, but some components may have survived re-entry,” the agency stated in an update to Swift’s blog Wednesday afternoon.

items.title: This Overlooked Linux mv Option Replaces Three Commands With One
items.summary: Every Linux user has done the three-step dance at least once. You want to swap two files, so you move the first one to a temporary name, move the second one into its place, and then move the temporary file back. Ever felt that this is a bit... clumsy? And for a moment, one of your files simply doesn't exist. That doesn't feel right! Since version 9.5, GNU coreutils has a better way: mv --exchange. In this article, I'll show you what it does, how to check if your system has it, where it actually helps, and the mistake I made the first time I used it on directories.

items.title: Winter Hiking Boots FAQ
items.summary: If you plan to hike this winter, buy insulated, waterproof winter hiking boots to protect your feet and keep them warm. Regular hiking boots intended for three-season conditions, mids, or trail runners lack enough insulation and may not stay waterproof in wet snow, puddles, or slush. Even regular leather hiking boots treated with waterproofing products … com.

items.title: Republican Mark Lamb moves ahead in race for Arizona’s 5th Congressional District
items.summary: Republican Mark Lamb moved ahead of Democrat Elizabeth Lee as more results were tallied in Arizona’s 5th Congressional District race. Lee held a surprising lead of 4 percentage points in the GOP stronghold after initial results were released on Election Day. But Lamb took the lead as more votes were tabulated and held a 51.1% to 48.8% advantage, a difference of 6,412 votes, as of Wednesday evening. The open seat covers much of the East Valley and parts of Pinal County, including Queen Creek and Apache Junction.

items.title: Trace Gas Orbiter discovers potential evidence of volcanic activity on Mars via atmospheric observations
items.summary: Using data from the joint European and Russian ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter at Mars, an international team of scientists has discovered new evidence of volcanic activity on the red planet’s surface. Newly formed fissures in the surface seemingly allow gases from subsurface volcanic hotspots to rise to the Martian surface. These gases are primarily composed of hydrogen chloride, which the Trace Gas Orbiter first detected in the Martian atmosphere in 2021. Hydrogen chloride is normally found within magmatic vents in volcanic regions on Earth, suggesting the same might be occurring on Mars.

items.title: Something strange is happening with Android TV remotes, and it’s driving users crazy
items.summary: TL;DR Some Android TV users report that pressing Home on the TV remote now selects the top navigation bar instead of their favorite apps. Reports span NVIDIA Shield TV devices, while our own observations suggest the behavior varies across Android TV hardware. Google hasn’t explained the apparent change, and we’re asking readers to help establish how widespread it is. There’s a special kind of frustration that comes from a button doing exactly what it says, just not what your fingers remember. For some Android TV owners, that button is Home, and a seemingly invisible change is sending their carefully rehearsed remote-control routines off-script.

items.title: As voters seek relief from high living costs in election, economist weighs in on affordability reality
items.summary: For Ersa Divina Gracia, the pressure of higher living costs is visible in her shopping cart. This is like $150, Divina Gracia, Phoenix said, explaining that the same amount of money used to fill her cart. Affordability weighed on her mind when she voted. "It's really, really, you know, way, way, way different. We're lost now, gasoline," Divina Gracia said. Other Phoenix consumers described similar concerns about their everyday expenses. Its hitting us. Were skipping some things that we used to buy, Sue Grace, Phoenix, said.

items.title: Two competitive Phoenix City Council seats headed for a runoff
items.summary: From the stories making headlines to the restaurants, music and culture that make Phoenix one of a kind, New Times is there. Help us raise $25,000 by December 31 to keep independent local journalism going strong in 2027. The Phoenix City Council is bringing in some fresh meat. We’re just not quite sure what kind yet. Shiny fresh faces fought over two term-limited seats — District 4 and District 2 — but neither had a candidate with enough votes to win outright on Election Night. Instead, it looks like the top candidates in both races will have to fight it out again on March 9 in a runoff to find out who really comes out on top.

items.title: Virtual power plants can help avoid overbuilt grid if AI boom goes bust
items.summary: Nobody really knows how much power the data center boom will need — and that’s putting utilities in a tough spot. If they underinvest in power plants and the grid, economic growth and energy reliability will suffer. But if they overinvest, Americans may pay for infrastructure nobody needs. One way to blunt these…

items.title: Linux 7.4 Showing Few Performance Gains With Initial Benchmarks On AMD Ryzen Threadripper
items.summary: In the first round of benchmarking the in-development Linux 7.4 kernel there are some performance improvements -- and some small regressions -- worth noting over the current Linux 7.3 stable kernel. This first round of Linux 7.4 kernel benchmarking was on a System76 Thelio Major workstation with AMD Ryzen Threadripper 9980X.

items.title: Mir 2.31 Released With Expanded Wayland Protocol Support
items.summary: Mir 2.31 is now available as the latest feature release for this Canonical/Ubuntu solution for providing C++ libraries to build Wayland-based shells. Mir 2.31 expands its Wayland protocol coverage with adding experimental support for ext_foreign_buffer_v1. With this a client can attach an opaque buffer with contents maintained by the compositor from an image-capture source. Mir 2.31 also adds unstable xdg-decoration protocol version 2 support and experimental mir_shell_v1 also at version 2. This Mir update also now allows its magnifier to be freely-positioned, adds display configuration data, and provides input and application authorization support.

items.title: Buckeye victim defends fiancé accused of planning her attack
items.summary: BUCKEYE, AZ (AZFamily) — A woman who was attacked in Buckeye last month defended her partner in court Wednesday against accusations that he planned the attack online. Police said the woman’s fiancé, 23-year-old Zarian Dyer, plotted the Oct. 16 attack with Adrian Ayala, 20, over Reddit. She told a judge that’s not true, despite police saying they have messages and other evidence tying Dyer to the plot. “My partner was forced to deal with false accusations fabricated by the defendant during his frantic attempt to make excuses,” she told the court, referring to claims by Ayala that her partner sent him.

items.title: ‘Chainsmoker Cat’ Missed Netflix’s Global Top 10, But Surging Manga Sales Could Save Season 2
items.summary: rst season, yet fans are still waiting to hear about a renewal. With roughly a third of the manga adapted, Bibury Animation Studios has plenty of source material left to adapt. And while it didn’t exactly dominate Netflix, the series sparked massive online discussion and a huge increase in manga sales, leaving hopeful fans eager for a second season. Chainsmoker Cat is a Japanese anime series based on the Japanese manga Yani Neko by author and illustrator NyanNyanFactory. Biburry Animation Studios animates the series, with Taku Kimura and Takashi Aoshima directing.

items.title: 19-year-old Democrat set to become next Maricopa County Clerk of the Superior Court
items.summary: Democrat Sebastian Matta, a 19-year-old sophomore at Arizona State University, is set to defeat Republican Jeff Dial in the race for Maricopa County Clerk of the Superior Court. In a statement posted to social media Wednesday afternoon, Dial appeared to concede, stating he hoped the clerk’s office had a successful future and thanking everyone who helped with his campaign and the election. To everyone who volunteered and helped out — thank you. And to everyone in Maricopa County who worked hard on Election Day to run a good election: this great state runs on people like you.

items.title: Heavy-Lift Drone Completes 50-Mile Flight in Indiana Corridor
items.summary: A Purdue University-owned Windracers ULTRA drone completed a flight of more than 50 miles beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) during the opening of Indiana’s new unmanned aircraft test site on Oct. 29. The flight took place at Terre Haute Regional Airport and was the first BVLOS operation within the state’s 200-plus-mile drone corridor, according to Windracers. The aircraft also demonstrated a parachute cargo drop during the event, which attracted state and federal officials, including FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford.

items.title: Arizona Democrats promise major changes to ESA voucher program after big election wins
items.summary: Democratic lawmakers say they plan to push income limits, tighter safety requirements and a state audit of Arizona's billion-dollar school voucher program.

items.title: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
items.summary: China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now. Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports. That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program.

items.title: Ricursive AI Releases Ripple-65B Preview: A 65B Dense Open-Weight Model Scoring 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1
items.summary: Ricursive Intelligence just released Ripple-65B Preview. Ripple-65B Preview is a 65B dense open-weight model from Ricursive, pretrained from scratch for agentic coding. It is a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind Ricursive’s AI chip design platform. The main claim: 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, the top self-reported score among US open-weight models. Every MoE rival it beats on that test carries 501B to 975B total parameters. TL;DR Size: 65B dense (65B active), pretrained on 12T tokens, up to 1M context.

items.title: ‘Blue Eye Samurai’ Season 2 Officially Sets January 19, 2027 Release Date on Netflix
items.summary: Netflix, we finally have an exact date for its return. Netflix has confirmed that the six-episode second season will arrive on January 19, 2027, narrowing down the January window revealed at Anime NYC back in August. Alongside the date, Netflix has shared a new first-look video and a batch of new images of Mizu’s bloody quest continuing in London. Season 1 dropped on November 3, 2023, so by the time season 2 lands, fans will have waited a little over three years and two months for new episodes. It has been a long road.

items.title: A Virtual Lifeless Earth Will Help Scientists Find Life on Exoplanets
items.summary: Researchers have created a model lifeless Earth that couples the atmosphere with interior planetary processes. The model can reproduce Earth's modern habitable state without including life, showing that a planet that appears habitable isn't necessarily inhabited. The tool will be useful when and if the Habitable Worlds Observatory is launched, by helping identify false positives.

items.title: Let there be light—novel AI framework runs on optical hardware
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly pervasive and capable but is also very hungry for power. Researchers, including those at the University of Tokyo, have developed a new approach to building physics-based AI—systems that use the natural behavior of physical systems to process information—that dramatically reduces the amount of computation required for them to run. The approach simplifies both how these systems learn and how they are structured. It was demonstrated using an optical computing system that processes information with light and could help pave the way toward faster and more energy-efficient AI hardware.

items.title: Omarchy 4.5 Released With Apple Silicon Support, More Desktop Customizations
items.summary: Omarchy 4.5 is out today as a big feature update to this Arch Linux based operating system. Omarchy is the project's first release where they have expanded beyond x86_64 to now support some AArch64 hardware too. Apple Silicon is a primary support target along with NVIDIA N1X laptops while the Snapdragon X laptop support is forthcoming. Omarchy 4.5 is reported to work on M1 / M2 / M3 and Neo MacBook hardware. This builds off the work done by Asahi Linux and others. On the NVIDIA ARM side, in addition to N1X there is also DGX Spark desktop support.

items.title: Tempe Town Lake turns into a rushing river after record fall storms
items.summary: SRP says the flood is the biggest on the Salt and Verde rivers since 1993. Flows are falling, but there’s no date for boaters to return.

items.summary: Learn how Google Antigravity and our Cheminformatics Skills accelerate drug discovery workflows, search compounds, and propose novel rigidified macrocycles.

items.title: No injuries reported after small plane makes hard landing at Phoenix Sky Harbor
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Five people walked away with no injuries after a pilot made a hard landing Wednesday night at Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. It happened near 24th Street and Interstate 10 on the southwest side of the airport around 7 p.m. Firefighters said that when they arrived, they found a small plane with five people on board. All five people told firefighters they were OK. Video from the scene shows a plane on its belly but no visible damage. Phoenix Fire did not provide details about what led up to the hard landing.

items.title: Sinkhole in Scottsdale reduces traffic to single lane
items.summary: Southbound Hayden Road is reduced to one lane between the Loop 101 and Mayo Boulevard, Scottsdale police say.

items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
items.summary: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan. For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket. The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause?

items.title: JoAnna Mendoza maintains lead over incumbent Juan Ciscomani in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District
items.summary: Democrat JoAnna Mendoza holds a lead over Republican Rep. Juan Ciscomani in the race for Arizona’s 6th Congressional District seat. As of Wednesday evening, the results showed the challenger leading by 8.1 percentage points, 53% to 44.9%, a difference of 24,976 votes. Mendoza declared victory Tuesday night, and Decision Desk HQ called the race in her favor. But The Associated Press has not yet made a call in the contest. The southern Arizona district, which includes much of eastern Tucson and parts of Pima, Pinal, Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties, was expected to be one of the most competitive House races in the country, but it’s not turning out that way.

items.title: Rep. Eli Crane leading Jonathan Nez in Arizona’s 2nd Congressional District
items.summary: Republican incumbent Eli Crane is leading challenger Jonathan Nez in the race for Arizona’s 2nd Congressional District. The race for the district seat started as a nail-biter as Crane and Nez were only separated by about 1,400 votes in the initial wave of results Tuesday night. However, by Wednesday evening, the results showed Crane with 143,106 votes, or 49.5%, and Nez with 140,871 votes, or 48.7%. The race is a rematch of 2024, when Crane carried the district by about 9 percentage points. President Donald Trump won the same district by about 15 points that year.

items.title: Ai2 and Google collaborate on a new generation of climate models
items.summary: With funding from Google.org and technical support from Google Research, Ai2 is developing NeuralGCM+, an open-source model designed to combine physics and AI to simulate the atmosphere and ocean together for faster, more reliable long-term climate projections.

items.title: Jeff Dial concedes to 19-year-old ASU student Sebastian Matta in Maricopa County court clerk race
items.summary: Republican Jeff Dial, a former state senator, has called Democrat Sebastian Matta to concede the Maricopa County clerk of Superior Court race, both candidates tell me. As of 5pm Wednesday evening, Matta held a 53.4% to 46.6% lead according to the Maricopa County election results website. Matta, a 19-year-old Arizona State University student, will lead the clerk's office in the nation's fourth-largest county. "I mean, I only got a campaign manager like three weeks ago," Matta said. Matta graduated high school last year and studies philosophy of law, politics and morality at Arizona State.

items.title: KDE Gear 26.08.3 Released with Numerous Application Bug Fixes
items.summary: The KDE Project has announced KDE Gear 26.08.3, the third maintenance update to the 26.08 series of its application collection. One of the applications receiving the most fixes is the Kdenlive video editor. The update addresses crashes related to nonlinear fades, clip pasting, proxy generation, and project creation. It also improves recovery of corrupted project files and ensures autosave files are preserved when saving a project fails. Additional Kdenlive fixes target rendering, including incorrect scaling values in the render dialog, low disk space warnings, and render jobs incorrectly marked as running.

items.title: Arizona Democrats and Republicans reflect on power shift after ‘blue wave’
items.summary: PHOENIX – It was a rough night for Arizona Republicans on Election Day. The top six statewide races are expected to all go blue, and the state Legislature could see a historic shift toward being majority Democrat, which hasn’t happened in decades. Democratic and Republican leaders in the Legislature are now navigating what this historic shift in control looks like and how they’ll target affordability, education and water as they enter a new political balance. The Associated Press called the Arizona governor, secretary of state and attorney general races for Democrats.

items.title: Linehouse reimagines industrial aesthetics for Jen Hangzhou hotel in Kohn Pedersen Fox-designed building
items.summary: International studio Linehouse has completed the interiors of the Jen hotel in Hangzhou, China, which features details that nod to local craft and the area's industrial heritage. The hotel, which is owned by the Shangri-La Hotel Group, is located along Hangzhou's Dongxin River in an urban setting and flanked by two former industrial factory compounds. Plans and drawings Previous Next Plans and drawings Close The 18-floor hotel building was designed by US architecture firm Kohn Pedersen Fox, using steel, grey brick and glass to reference the site's industrial past.

items.title: Some AI bots work harder to defy stereotypes, study finds
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs), the technology that powers tools like Gemini and ChatGPT, are more nuanced than ever. But that doesn't mean they aren't biased. Some models are more prejudiced than others, a Rutgers University researcher has found.

items.title: Scare at Sky Harbor Wednesday evening as plane experiences hard landing on runway
items.summary: A plane landed on its belly at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. The plane was carrying five people, authorities say.

items.title: ‘It’s a daunting task’: Democrats prep to lead Arizona legislature for first time in 60 years
items.summary: For the first time in six decades, Democrats control the Arizona legislature and will be able to turn their policy priorities into state law. But doing so without ostracizing the Republican and independent voters who helped elect them may prove difficult as the party grapples with governing a state where Republican voters still outnumber registered Democrats. Tuesday’s election was a boon for Democrats up and down the ballot. The state’s three top Democratic incumbents easily trounced their GOP challengers, and the party is poised to wrest two extra congressional seats and the Superintendent of Public Instruction’s Office from Republicans.

items.title: Six standout projects unveiled at Designart Tokyo 2026
items.summary: As the 10th anniversary edition of Designart Tokyo gets underway, Jane Englefield reports on six highlights from the citywide festival of Japanese creativity. Designart Tokyo opened on 30 October and will remain open across Tokyo until 8 November. Around 150 projects by exhibitors from 13 countries are on display at various galleries and other pop-up locations throughout the city. This year's main exhibition venue is the former site of the Tokyo Expressway, also known as the KK Line, a portion of which is now an elevated park in the heart of Ginza.

items.title: Chatbots with personality? How AI describes itself and judges us
items.summary: Texts generated by large language models, or AI-powered chatbots, exhibit characteristic "personality" traits. Such chatbots can also identify individual personality traits in texts. However, humans are more reliable at distinguishing between human-written and AI-generated texts, according to researchers at the Institute of Psychology at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU).

items.title: Black Clover Season 2 Dominates Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 Schedule With New Streaming Milestone
items.summary: It turns out Black Clover has been absolutely dominating Crunchyroll’s new slate of Fall 2026 anime releases as it has hit a new streaming milestone for October. This past October kicked off a new wave of anime that began their runs for the Fall, and the season has been largely dominated by returning franchises coming back for new episodes. But even with all of that competition, it’s been made clear that there’s one returning franchise in particular that fans have been most anticipating this Fall.

items.title: 2026 Arizona ballot measure results: Voters approve at least 4 propositions
items.summary: Arizona voters were asked to weigh in on eight propositions as part of Tuesday’s midterm general election. The statewide ballot measures covered a variety of hot-button issues, including election laws, transgender athletes and photo radar cameras. As of Wednesday evening, four measures were projected to pass and one was projected to fail. Of the three that were still too close to call, the yes votes were leading for one: Prop 141 on banning vehicle miles traveled taxes. No votes led in the other two: Prop 144 on voter ID and other election reforms, and Prop 320 on school district spending requirements.

items.title: "Commitment of the design community remains strong" say Ukrainian design week founders
items.summary: This year's Ukrainian Design and Innovation Week went ahead despite Russian strikes affecting the local design community. The event's founders share their top picks of exhibited brands that have continued production amid the war. "The reality of operating in Ukraine remains extremely challenging," Ukrainian Design and Innovation Week founders Anatolii and Kateryna Roskovshenko told Dezeen. Photography Previous Next Photography Close Ukraine has endured the constant threat of Russian bombardment for over four years, and recent months have been increasingly deadly for civilians, according to Human rights group Amnesty International.

items.title: Design Doha Biennial 2026 set to explore how traditional crafts can shape the future of design
items.summary: Design Doha Biennial 2026 opens in Doha, Qatar, today, bringing together more than 19 exhibitions, five installations and over 80 designers, featuring projects that use traditional water systems and building techniques to tackle urban heat. Following a postponement earlier this year due to war in the Gulf, the event will now run from today until 31 January 2027, with its opening programme taking place from 5 to 7 November. For the event Doha 's historic neighbourhood of Fereej Al Asmakh has been transformed into an exhibition venue to showcase contemporary architecture and design from across the Middle East, north Africa and south Asia.

items.title: New Medieval Books: The Crusader Storm
items.summary: When the Crusaders arrived in the Holy Land at the end of the 11th century, they entered a region shaped by numerous peoples, kingdoms and competing political interests. This book takes a broader look at the conflicts, alliances and political struggles unfolding across the eastern Mediterranean during this period.

items.title: Home Assistant's 2026.11 update is packed with features and a brand new Marketplace
items.summary: As Home Assistant users, we’re spoiled by the project’s clockwork release cycle that sees a new major release arrive every month without fail. But not all updates are built equal, and November 2026 brings a very special community effort into the core release. The Home Assistant Marketplace makes its debut in Home Assistant 2026.11, bringing every feature of the Home Assistant Community Store (HACS) into the main release without the need to install anything extra. For those unaware, the Home Assistant Community Store is an optional enhancement for Home Assistant 2026.10 and earlier that makes it easy to install and manage community-created add-ons.

items.title: What I learned driving the Slate electric truck prototype
items.summary: If my 45-minute drive yesterday morning is anything to go by, I think Slate Auto will have quite the hit on its hands. The startup had one of its prototype trucks in town and asked if I wanted to check it out—no jumping on a plane or having to spend yet another night in an interchangeable hotel room, just a drive from southwest DC to Rockville, Maryland. Easy-peasy. The prototype truck had been well-used, with almost 6,000 miles (9,656 km) showing on the small and minimalist but very legible digital display that also shows your speed and, if you engage reverse, the backup camera.

items.title: The LEGO-like co-op pirate roguelite Sink My Bricks! looks like chaotic fun
items.summary: Everything looks like it's made out of LEGO-styled bricks in the co-op pirate roguelite Sink My Bricks! A new announcement from developer Sleepy Amigos, it was originally teased as Shiver My Bricks! The sea, the ships, the islands, the creatures, you - everything is built from bricks and anything can be destroyed. It really looks like a lot of fun! Playable solo or with a total of four people in online co-op this is sure to be a blast. Together, players raid archipelagos, board enemy ships and patch holes in their own hull in the middle of a fight.

items.title: Jake Gyllenhaal's 124-Minute Sci-Fi Disaster Movie Is Officially Netflix's Biggest Streaming Hit
items.summary: In 2004, "The Day After Tomorrow" clumsily delivered a message about climate change via a movie in which Dennis Quaid and Jake Gyllenhaal try to save the world from a new ice age. The questionable part of the film was the science, which as NASA Goddard Space Flight Center meteorologist J. Marshall Shepherd told USA Today, warranted "a D minus or an F." Otherwise, "The Day After Tomorrow" was a grand old time at the movies, and now it seems modern audiences are having a similarly wonderful time with the end of the world over on Netflix.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI introduces its National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint to protect local resources, create jobs, and guide responsible AI infrastructure development.

items.title: Fraunhofer develops tool for battery recycling
items.summary: Fraunhofer FFB and RWTH Aachen University have developed an evaluation model for the recycling of lithium-ion batteries. It allows different processes to be compared in terms of their costs and CO₂ emissions. The calculation model is designed to help recycling companies, technology providers and battery manufacturers evaluate different recycling processes on a uniform basis – both economically and ecologically. A recent study by the EU research project Safeloop highlighted the significant economic challenges in battery recycling.

items.title: Tesla opens new engineering centre in Berlin-Köpenick
items.summary: Tesla has opened its new development center in Berlin-Köpenick. Engineers and technicians will work there on new vehicles, engines, and materials, as well as research and testing. The location will bring together 250 employees who previously worked at various sites.

items.title: Grid pressures accelerate utility solar and storage integration
items.summary: During a panel discussion at pv magazine USA Week 2026, industry leaders from OCI Energy, Array Technologies, and Trina Storage examined how utility-scale solar and battery storage have become the dominant foundation of U.S. power generation. Accounting for over 90% of all new capacity added to the domestic grid, solar-plus-storage assets are being deployed rapidly to meet massive load growth driven primarily by data center expansions. Tax credit deadlines and capacity drivers Developer demand this year was heavily influenced by safe harbor and tax credit timelines, forcing companies to secure key equipment well in advance.

items.title: Watch live: NASA installs final roll-out solar array on International Space Station in spacewalk
items.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk are completing U.S. Spacewalk 101 to install and deploy the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA). The extravehicular activity follows the successful installation of the seventh array on Oct. 29. The installation concludes a five-year augmentation program designed to upgrade the station’s legacy power system.

items.title: Why Did One Muslim Community Survive in Medieval Christian Europe?
items.summary: For more than 600 years, a Muslim community has maintained its presence in a region of Europe ruled for centuries by Catholic monarchs. A new study examines how the Lithuanian-Polish Tatars survived when other Muslim communities faced expulsion, forced conversion and persecution. Published in the journal Nationalities Papers, the study examines the history of the Lithuanian-Polish Tatars, also known as the Lipka Tatars, whose ancestors settled in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania during the late fourteenth century.

items.summary: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 is here! This version brings you Air, as well as an extension for Cursor and VS Code, debugging improvements, and support for the latest technologies in the Java ecosystem. items.title: What Class A reveals about solar PV module fire performance
items.summary: While two solar modules can carry the same Class A designation, they can differ in their fire performance. The shared label can conceal differences that matter for the safety of the building below. Class A is a defined classification reached through prescribed test criteria, and any Class A claim must identify the standard used. It should not automatically be interpreted as “fireproof”, nor does the classification itself tell a potential user how far beyond the pass threshold a particular solar module performed.

items.title: Rare Medieval Warship Wreck Investigated in Sweden
items.summary: Archaeologists in Sweden have uncovered new details about a remarkably well-preserved 500-year-old shipwreck that may be the oldest known medieval warship built in Sweden or Denmark. Their discoveries include evidence of the ship’s kitchen, rigging equipment and an unusual method of mast construction. Marine archaeologists from Vrak Museum and Södertörn University made the discoveries during a recent underwater excavation near Häringe, south of Stockholm. The shipwreck, known as Vrak 5, dates to the 1480s and measures approximately 35 metres (115 feet) in length.

items.title: Night, Rain, Piper Seneca
items.summary: As a member of the Aviation Safety Council, we have monthly safety meetings where we discuss issues and incidents involving flight training crews ‘weather, technical issues, and human factors. I recently asked myself what kind of skills and knowledge would be useful in this type of situation, and how to remain calm and make the right decisions. As a Part 141 flight school, we have an FAA-approved Multi-Engine Add-On course that includes night flight hours in multi-engine aircraft. We carefully schedule night flights and avoid advanced maneuvers.

items.title: Teens worldwide aren't getting enough exercise -- especially girls
items.summary: The World Health Organization recommends adolescents spend at least one hour a day exercising enough to basically break a sweat — a brisk walk or a more intense pick-up soccer game. Lot's of research suggests this level of activity is crucial for supporting growing bodies and minds. But new global data suggests only a small minority of kids and teens get that much. In fact, one in four report not hitting 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous exercise any day of the week, according to a new study in The Lancet Global Health.

items.title: High gas prices are pumping up used EV sales: these are FLYING off the lot
items.summary: A new car affordability crisis and punishing gas prices are driving an unprecedented number of used car buyers to consider going electric, and that increased demand without a corresponding increase in supply means these used EVs are flying off dealer lots. more…

items.title: VW And Skoda EV Owners Have Waited Years For Battery Preconditioning. It's Finally Coming
items.summary: Volkswagen and Skoda are adding a much-needed battery pre-heating feature to the oldest ID.4, ID.5, and Enyaq EVs on the road. Over 200,000 cars will get an over-the-air software update starting in the second half of November, 2027. The update will be rolled out in stages, and there are some prerequisites to keep in mind. The first Volkswagen ID.4 and Skoda Enyaq electric crossovers to roll off the assembly lines back in 2020 marked a big step for the two automakers, but owners quickly faced an uncomfortable truth: their high-voltage batteries could not be preconditioned for fast charging, which resulted in longer-than-expected charging times during cold weather.

items.title: The 50 Best Restaurants 2026: The Full List of Winners
items.summary: Tonight, the 50 Best Restaurants 2026 were announced at a ceremony in Lima, Peru, with Basque Country restaurant Asador Etxebarri crowned the new top slot on the list. Bangkok tasting counter Gaggan was ranked No. 2, Copenhagen’s immersive, 50-course experience Alchemist was No. 3, Mexico City’s Quintonil No. 4, and Hong Kong’s Wing No. 5, shuffling most of the top rankings from last year. New York City’s Atomix was the only U.S. restaurant to make the 50 Best Restaurants.

items.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
items.summary: Running a modern research laboratory requires more than maintaining sophisticated instruments. Researchers need to complete training, obtain access, schedule and operate equipment, navigate billing, and more. For large, shared facilities, coordinating these activities across hundreds of instruments and thousands of users can be a significant undertaking. As research becomes increasingly interdisciplinary, another challenge is emerging: finding the right capability in the first place. Addressing these challenges was a central theme of the 2026 NEMO User Meeting, hosted by MIT.nano Oct.

items.title: Linux 7.4’s Merge Window is Huge, and Linus Says it Might Not Just Be AI
items.summary: The story starts when Linus Torvalds opened the Linux 7.4 merge window more than two weeks ago when he was headed out for his annual family vacation, resulting in some temporary disruptions to his work. He warned that his schedule would be unusual and that merging might need an extra week, but RC1 still arrived according to the usual two-week schedule. None of that made the window any smaller. By his count, it brought in almost 20,000 commits, where 15,000 or so is the usual number, while the shortlog alone ran to 24,000 lines.

items.title: Hobbs, Giles celebrate historic Arizona victory
items.summary: Hundreds gathered in west Phoenix as Gov. Katie Hobbs and Lt. Gov.-elect John Giles celebrated election wins and an upcoming legislative majority.

items.title: This Startup Wants To Turn Teslas Into Anything, From 11-Seat Minibuses To Pickups
items.summary: A Wisconsin startup wants to turn old or wrecked Tesla EVs into pretty much anything. The Hoffman Badger made its debut at the SEMA show in Las Vegas as a minibus. Sales are expected to start next year, with prices slotting between the Slate Truck and Tesla Cybertruck. The slightly dorky vehicle you see here can use Tesla’s Superchargers and so-called Full-Self Driving (Supervised) driver assistance system. And no, your eyes are not deceiving you—this is not a Tesla. At least, not at first glance.

items.title: Ready to Graduate From Tent Camping? What to Know Before Buying Your First RV
items.summary: Tent camping has a lot going for it. Your setup fits in the back of a car, you can squeeze into smaller campsites, and there’s nothing quite like unzipping the tent to a mountain, lake, or forest just outside. But there may come a trip when sleeping on the ground loses some of its charm. Maybe you’ve packed up one too many wet tents. Maybe your family needs more room. Or maybe you’re simply ready for a bathroom, a kitchen, or a mattress that doesn’t need to be inflated before bed. An RV can add those comforts while keeping the outdoors at the center of the trip.

items.title: Democratic victories cloud outlook for AI data center rollout
items.summary: Strong wins for Democratic candidates threaten the prospects for energy-guzzling data centers in key U.S. states, potentially slowing the AI rollout that has carried Wall Street forward over the past four years.

items.title: GM is recalling more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs over a brake software defect
items.summary: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking. The recall comes after a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq ran into a garage (at a low speed). On April 10, 2026, a GM tech expert submitted a report to GM’s Speak Up for Safety (SUFS) program for review. After internal testing, GM was able to replicate the glitch, similar to a recall it issued in 2024. GM said the issue stems from a software glitch with the brake system control module (BSCM) that can cause a temporary loss of braking while driving under certain conditions.

items.title: Great Art Explained Traces the Incredible Story of Henri Matisse’s ‘The Red Studio’
items.summary: In today’s art world, provocation and controversy are part and parcel of the market. Think recent pieces like Maurizio Cattelan’s “Comedian,” a.k.a. the duct-taped banana, or Damien Hirst’s diamond- and platinum-coated 18th-century human skull titled “For the Love of God.” And while art has never been immune to controversy, it hasn’t always been, let’s say, expected. At the turn of the 20th century, art—especially the “high” mediums of painting and sculpture—were viewed and taught through the lens of deeply ingrained conventions about what made art good.

items.title: Ford Fathom EV pickup prices will range from $28,350 to the high $30Ks
items.summary: Ford’s upcoming Fathom electric pickup will be among the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at $28,350. Even pricier trims will start at under $40,000. After announcing the name of its new midsize electric pickup this summer, Ford said the Fathom will start at just $28,350 for the standard-range model. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee, prices will start at under $30,000. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Jim Farley said the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle off the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

items.title: The New Bon Appétit Cooking App Is Here!
items.summary: Dear Bon Appétit readers, Every day we offer you must-make dinners from our Test Kitchen, inspiring menus for every occasion, showstopping desserts, and clever cocktails. This holiday season, we are thrilled to bring you all the cookies, juicy roasts, sheet-pan dinners, and much more in the new Bon Appétit app. This exciting new tool is more than a digital version of our extensive archive of recipes. The app is designed to help you plan and pull off great meals, whether you’re a novice cook or a seasoned chef.

items.title: Mexican Seafood and Natural Wines Are in the Spotlight at This New NYC Restaurant
items.summary: Known for their roasted and slow-cooked meats at Taqueria Ramirez, Tania Apolinar and Giovanni Cervantes partnered with chef Carlos Barrera to open a new seafood-focused wine bar this year. Here’s what a full day of prep looks like at El Camarón Peludo in the West Village. First, fresh shrimp from Sinaloa, Mexico; Ecuador; and more locales are de-shelled and de-veined for three central shrimp dishes. Then, Cervantes starts the fresh salsa for the day, taste testing and comparing each batch to the salsa from last week to make sure the flavor is consistent.

items.title: Together AI Releases Together Compiler: Agents Make Inference Up to 2.6x Faster
items.summary: Together AI has introduced Together Compiler (TKCC), an agent-driven system that keeps re-optimizing inference as production traffic changes. Together Compiler already runs on several of Together’s serverless endpoints. The core claim for developers: an engine tuned once goes stale, so tuning should never stop. TL;DR System: It is an optimization system, tested on Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash and Llama 1B. Runs on: NVIDIA B200, B300, GB300, H100, AMD MI355X and AWS Trainium2.

items.title: Ancient coins suggest influential Iron Age king was female
items.summary: Bournemouth University (BU) archaeological research has revealed that Iron Age British ruler "Verica," who was central to the Roman invasion of Britain in A.D. 43, was in fact a woman. This discovery rewrites the history of early Roman Britain.

items.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
items.summary: Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved. Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on oil prices. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase".

items.title: Here's what the Democratic election rout could mean for the U.S. economy
items.summary: The Democratic midterm election sweep could result in changes in economic policies related to trade, spending priorities and artificial intelligence. But the biggest forces shaping the economy aren't going to change just because the party in power did. Affordability pressures, heavy levels of government spending and growth that is dependent on the artificial-intelligence tailwind are likely to persist, economists say. And all of those factors pose risks to the economy. "It's in a very kind of fragile place, and I don't know that it would take a lot to push the economy off the rails, and recession becomes a much greater risk," said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics.

items.title: Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war, warns inflation will near 5%
items.summary: The Bank of England announced its first interest rate hike in over three years on Thursday, raising its key rate by 25 basis points to 4%. The widely anticipated move marked the bank's first hike since Aug. 2023, and made it the last major central bank to embark on a tightening cycle since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran eight months ago. The majority of the bank's Monetary Policy Committee voted for the quarter-point hike, with the motion passing by 8 votes to 1. The dissenting member voted to raise the bank's key interest rate by 50 basis points to 4.25%.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience.

items.title: A 7,000-year-old piece of leather reveals a deep history of Spanish goats
items.summary: Ancient DNA reveals that denizens of the Iberian Peninsula made leather from domestic goats as far back as 7,000 years ago, according to a study published Nov. 4, 2026, in the journal PLOS One by Jolijn A. M. Erven of University College Dublin, Ireland, and colleagues.

items.title: Microglia drive excessive iron transfer in Parkinson's disease models
items.summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition associated with worsening tremors, slowed movements, changes in walking and speech, muscle rigidity and postural instability. Many of its symptoms are associated with a progressive loss of dopamine-producing neurons in a brain region called the substantia nigra pars compacta.

items.title: Hot homes cause heart strain in older Australians
items.summary: With summer fast approaching, along with the inevitable heat and humidity, new Griffith University research offers a timely reminder about the dangers of hot homes and the serious strain they can place on older Australians when the indoor temperature exceeds 26°C (79 degrees Fahrenheit).

items.title: Ancient DNA traces origins of English, German and Scandinavian languages
items.summary: English, German, Dutch and the Scandinavian languages are all members of the Germanic language group, spoken by hundreds of millions of people today. But where did these languages come from?

items.title: Trump accepts election results as Republicans face midterm reckoning | First Thing
items.summary: Criticism of US-Israel war on Iran seen as huge factor in Democrats’ sweeping victory. Plus, a spiky customer steps into a North Carolina bagel store Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. items.summary: It's been an extraordinary night for the Democrats in the US midterms. They have taken control of the Senate and the House of Representatives too. The results in the Senate are beyond what the Democrats would have expected. North Carolina was a likely pick-up but the previously deep red state of South Carolina was a huge shock and Kansas had not returned a Democratic senator since 1932. Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine also turned blue and the Democrats held Michigan. There are two seats remaining, Alaska and Mississippi, both are on a knife edge.

items.title: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
items.summary: People riding drunk or dangerously on e-bikes â and those who jump red lights - could face on-the-spot fines under plans to curb anti-social behaviour. Firms which run shared e-bike schemes will also be expected to manage their fleets better and provide designated parking areas to keep pavements safe. They could also be required to take out insurance so people can claim compensation if they are hit by someone on a shared bike. It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking â with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians.

items.title: Little Ice Age cooling in Europe may have raised the risk of rickets
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) England isn’t renowned for its weather. But just a few centuries ago, climate change–fueled conditions may have been so bad that they put children’s health at risk. Calcium mineralization in the teeth and skeletons of people who lived in rural northern England suggests that children growing up during the height of the Little Ice Age routinely developed vitamin D deficiencies, researchers report November 5 in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology.

items.title: The 2001 Debut of a $7.7B Fantasy Franchise Is a Streaming Hit Ahead of Its Controversial Reboot
items.summary: There are some franchises that really grab the attention of audiences young and old, becoming a phenomenal success and generating billions in box office receipts. The Harry Potter saga is a franchise that began as a simple story of a boy discovering his destiny as one of the greatest wizards in the world, but ended up becoming one of the biggest movie sagas of the 21st century. Now, just 14 years after the main movie saga came to an end, HBO are about to reboot the story with a lavish new TV series, even if some people are struggling to see why.

(This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook.

items.title: Advanced imaging uncovers genomic Achilles' heel that makes cancer cells vulnerable
items.summary: A small subset of vulnerable DNA sites can make cancer cells highly sensitive to targeted drugs called PARP inhibitors, a new study shows. Led by researchers at NYU Langone Health and its Perlmutter Cancer Center, the work revolved around failures of DNA to copy itself at certain sites in genetic chains, which it must do for cells to divide and multiply as part of healing and growth. Cancerous cells depend on protective mechanisms that have evolved to overcome these failures when they are triggered by cancer drugs.

items.title: Prehistoric 'giant rat' found in Thailand from fossil teeth
items.summary: A giant rodent weighing around 30 kilograms (66 pounds) roamed what is now southern Thailand 33 to 35 million years ago, scientists said, after identifying a previously unknown species from two fossilized teeth.

items.title: FAA orders Boeing 787 fuel tank inspections over lightning strike explosion risk
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of certain Boeing 787 Dreamliners after discovering that required manufacturing checks of fuel tank sealant were not completed or could not be verified, raising concerns about a potential fuel tank explosion during a lightning strike. The FAA airworthiness directive (AD), published November 2, 2026, applies to certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 aircraft. The FAA estimates that 60 US-registered aircraft are affected. The directive takes effect December 7, 2026.

items.title: Arizona ACA enrollees weigh coverage choices as premiums climb
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Hundreds of thousands of Arizonans are in the process of picking their health coverage through the ACA marketplace over the next few weeks, and many of those people are seeing higher premiums. Most insurers in Arizona raised rates between 25% to 30% for 2027, but in some cases people told Arizona’s Family their prices jumped even more. “It immediately became clear that the existing plan that my wife and I are on, they are increasing the monthly premium substantially,” Darryl Komesu said.

items.title: How Ancient Romans Engineered the Ultimate Death Arena
items.summary: The Roman Colosseum was much more than a grand architectural monument. Beneath the blood-soaked sands of the arena floor lay a terrifying labyrinth of mechanical terror. Known as the hypogeum, this subterranean network housed hundreds of slaves, wild beasts, and gladiators waiting for their violent end. Roman engineers designed an ingenious system of trapdoors, wooden elevators, and hidden pulleys to ensure that hungry lions or heavily armed warriors could spring into the sunlight at a moment’s notice.

items.title: 5,000-Year-Old Rock Art Found in Southern India
items.summary: CHENNAI, INDIA— News Today Net reports that rock art estimated to be 5,000 years old has been discovered in caves in the southern state of Tamil Nadu. The images are thought to have been drawn during the transition from hunting and gathering of the late Mesolithic period to early farming in the Neolithic period. They depict anthropomorphic figures, wild animals, dancing, and geometric designs. The Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology and the Archaeological Survey of India have been asked to list the site as a protected monument. To read about petroglyphs in India’s remote region of Ladakh, go to “ Himalayan High Art.”

items.title: Rare Strain of Leprosy Identified in Boat Burial
items.summary: CUXHAVEN GERMANY—According to a statement released by Kiel University, researchers from the Institute of Clinical Molecular Biology (IKMB) at Christian-Albrechts-University and the Lower Saxony Institute for Historical Coastal Research analyzed the remains of a man who was interred in a boat in the fifth century A.D. at the Fallward burial ground, which is located near Germany’s North Sea coast and the mouth of the Elbe River. The boat also contained items made of wood, pottery, and metal that were preserved in the site’s damp soil.

items.title: The Citadel Project is a Thief-inspired dark fantasy, survival-horror lite stealth-em-up with some lovely shadows set in a medieval megastructure
items.summary: You know, given the whole stealthy element of Thief-like immersive sims, I'm surprised there haven't been more of them with horror elements. There's Gloomwood, sure, but it's not as common as I'd like. That in turn then makes me curious about The Citadel Project, an immersive sim with some survival-horror elements set in a nasty, parasite-infected dark fantasy world, all apparently made by just one person.

items.title: Canva’s big layoffs say a lot about the AI design landscape
items.summary: The AI design giant Canva just announced the first-ever major round of layoffs in its 13-year history. As part of the restructuring, 1,271 people—around 22% of the company’s overall staff—will either be laid off, reassigned to new roles, or relocated to the company’s headquarters in Sydney, Australia. News of the layoffs was announced on November 3 (a perfect day to bury some bad news) in a press release from Canva cofounder and CEO Melanie Perkins.

items.title: For Talarico and Hinojosa, Whataburger Is a Perfectly Texas Place to Celebrate
items.summary: Like so many Texans on so many nights, Senator-elect James Talarico and Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa ended their evening at Whataburger. Late Tuesday night, after Talarico flipped a Senate seat for the Democrats and Hinojosa was elected the first Democratic governor of the state in more than three decades, the two sat down at an Austin-area location of Whataburger, the iconic regional fast food chain, to clink plastic orange-and-white-striped cups. It was a fitting setting for the pair, who played critical roles in the blue wave that swept the country in the midterm elections on Tuesday night.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.summary: OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. A newer internal model scores significantly higher on OpenAI's engineering benchmark, though the company isn't sharing details.

items.title: Six Flags warned that a roller coaster death will drag on fourth quarter earnings
items.summary: Six Flags Entertainment forecast fourth-quarter same-park adjusted EBITDA of $140 million to $150 million, versus $167 million in the year-ago period, after a fatal accident at Six Flags Over Georgia and bad weather left October softer than planned. EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

items.title: Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go?
items.summary: Interest rates have risen to 4% and the Bank of England has indicated there are more rises to come. The question is how many? There is a split on the rate-setting committee here. Three of the nine voting members referred to "rises" plural. One member voted for a bigger increase, to 4.25%. Three referred to just one more including governor Andrew Bailey. My read on this is that the expectation is for one more rise in February. Two and done, but it depends. It is painful for those on variable mortgages, but should not be seen as the start of a cycle of hikes.

items.title: coperni closes: revisiting the fashion label’s strangest experiments in design and technology
items.summary: look back on coperni’s most iconic moments Coperni, the Paris fashion label that once sprayed a dress directly onto Bella Hadid in front of a live audience, has ceased operations. Founded by Sébastien Meyer and Arnaud Vaillant, the label spent the past few years turning some radical ideas into wearable objects. Robot dogs walked alongside models, handbags were made from materials developed for space research, and a leather jacket became a functioning sound system. Much of this work involved collaborations with scientists and engineers, which brought onto the runway technologies rarely associated with fashion.

items.title: How the Phone Book Taught America to Ask for Answers
items.summary: For over a century, the physical phone book could be found everywhere, yet seemingly belonged nowhere: a book without a genre, at once mundane and mysterious, raising questions that vexed courts and corporations alike. In print, it’s all but vanished, though it lingers in the names of the websites and search engines that replaced it, the data they were built from, and the way we’ve learned to interact with information.

items.summary: As vibe coding moves from novelty to everyday practice, enterprises face a new problem: Machine-generated software still has to be maintained, governed and understood by people. items.title: making room for nature: the urban landscapes of kongjian yu

items.title: The Four-Color Theorem Has Haunted Mathematicians for Decades. It Just Got a Rare New Proof, but Some Still Long for a Simpler Solution
items.summary: The original version of this story appeared in Quanta magazine. Some math problems continue to haunt researchers long after they’ve been solved. A proof emerges, is even celebrated, and yet dissatisfaction lingers. Perhaps the argument is too convoluted—the hunt persists for the elusive one-page paper—or perhaps it fails to give a deeper theoretical insight into why something is true. items.title: The Power of the Roman People and the Hidden Democracy of SPQR
items.summary: Senatus Populusque Romanus means the “Senate and the People of Rome” in Latin, shortened to S.P.Q.R. This signature can be found on inscriptions and coins from the 1st century BC through the 4th century AD. This motto identified the two ruling bodies of Rome: the aristocratic Senate, Rome’s oligarchy, and the Roman people, who voted in the popular assembly as Rome’s sovereign body. items.title: South Korea tests Arctic shipping route amid Russia-West row
items.summary: A South Korean container ship completed a voyage to Western Europe through the Arctic Ocean off the northern coast of Russia in October, fueling Seoul's hopes of exploiting the route as a shortcut for trade. The ship made the round trip from Busan to Rotterdam in just 50 days, saving at least 10 days compared to the fastest travel times along the more commonly used Suez Canal route. The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is not only around 7,000 kilometers (4,350 miles) shorter, it also avoids the geopolitical flashpoint of the Middle East.

items.title: White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14
items.summary: A White House committee of inquiry postponed from Thursday to Dec. 14 a hearing with Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook for an investigation of whether allegations of false statements in mortgage applications warrant her firing by President Donald Trump, a White House official said Wednesday evening. But it was unclear if Cook, whom Trump unsuccessfully tried to fire in August 2025, would agree to attend. The official said the postponement came at the request of Cook. Her lawyer Abbe Lowell last month said questions about the committee's fairness and objectivity would have to be addressed before the hearing could occur.

items.title: Tight Quarters
items.summary: A puzzle from Alcuin of York’s Propositiones ad Acuendos Juvenes (Problems to Sharpen the Young), 9th century: “A man and his wife, each the weight of a loaded cart, who had two children each the weight of a small cart, needed to cross a river. However, the boat they came across could only carry the weight of one cart. Let him devise [a way] of crossing in order that the boat should not sink.” (The boat can bear the weight of two children or one adult.)

items.title: Wendy's rejects $1.4 billion takeover proposal from Nelson Peltz’s Trian
items.summary: Wendy's on Thursday said that it is rejecting a $1.4 billion takeover offer from a group of investors led by Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management. The group offered $7.35 per share in cash on Oct. 28 to take the struggling burger chain private. In addition to Trian, it included investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, plus Flynn Group, one of Wendy's largest franchisees. In February, Wendy's board formed a committee of independent directors to assess any potential bid from Trian in response to a regulatory filing from the firm.

items.title: FromSoftware-Inspired Dark Fantasy RPG ‘Queen’s Domain’ Available Now on PC, Consoles
items.summary: If you’re bummed about FromSoftware pushing the Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods to next year, Freshly Baked Games and publisher Future Friends Games have something to ease the pain. Inspired by the FromSoft classic (and precursor to Dark Souls ) in King’s Field, Freshly Baked Games’ dark fantasy RPG Queen’s Domain is available now on Steam, the Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series and PlayStation 5.

items.title: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
items.summary: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish. Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

items.title: The Man Who Risked His Life Mocking the Nazis: Read 96 Issues of His Underground Magazine, Created in Hiding During WWII
items.summary: The word zine, referring to a homemade magazine not distributed through the normal commercial channels, has a longer history than you might expect. Its earliest recorded uses date from 1946 in the world of pulp magazines, most often of the science-fiction variety. But just a year earlier, as it happens, one of the most historically notable zines avant la lettre concluded publication. The end of World War II had everything to do with it, since Het Onderwater-Cabaret, or The Underwater Cabaret, existed as a rebuke against the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands.

items.title: Florida Aviation Contractor Charged in Alleged Aircraft Records Theft
items.summary: A dispute over aircraft maintenance work has led to felony charges against a Florida man accused of removing records from a Piaggio Avanti after the airplane was moved to another aviation company. Kevin Vance McKamey, 61, of Largo, turned himself in Nov. 3 after investigators accused him of entering a Bayside Aviation hangar in Clearwater and taking aircraft records and a key. The alleged incident occurred Oct. 23, according to arrest affidavits. The airplane, a 2005 Piaggio Avanti valued at approximately $1.7 million, had been placed in Bayside Aviation’s care five days earlier.

items.title: Bomb threats hit at least 16 flights across Europe, trigger fighter escorts
items.summary: At least 16 passenger flights were targeted by bomb threats across Europe on November 5, 2026, prompting fighter escorts in France, Italy and Bulgaria, three diversions, and security inspections at airports across the continent. The alerts affected flights operated by Aer Lingus, Finnair, Ryanair, Wizz Air and LOT Polish Airlines. Searches completed by late morning in Rome, Prague and Brussels found no explosives, while checks were still underway elsewhere. The incidents came two days after a similar series of threats against Ryanair, Wizz Air, LOT and SAS flights on November 3, 2026, when searches also found no explosives.

items.title: Permanent daylight saving time has a dark side, scientists warn
items.summary: A new study warns that permanent daylight saving time could force American children to make at least 2 billion additional school commutes in darkness, potentially increasing safety risks and disrupting their biological clocks. Researchers found that fatal crashes involving school-aged pedestrians were roughly twice as likely during dark mornings as after sunrise.

items.title: Martin Scorsese Creates a List of 39 Essential Foreign Films for a Young Filmmaker
items.summary: As a young man, filmmaker Colin Levy got an opportunity of a lifetime. He got a one-on-one meeting with Martin Scorsese. After spending much of his time in high school making a five-minute short, Levy won the national YoungArts award — and, with it, the chance to chat with the guy who directed Goodfellas, Taxi Driver and Raging Bull. After getting a personal tour of Scorsese’s office and editing bays by none other than legendary editor Thelma Schoonmaker, Levy met the man himself. “It was a defining moment in my path as a filmmaker,” he later wrote on his blog.

items.summary: You’ve heard of Santa Claus, but have you heard of the Anti-Claus? items.title: MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures
items.summary: MIT scientists have challenged two decades of conventional thinking by discovering that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new ways to arrange nanoparticles. The breakthrough could lead to a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties and applications in electronics, medicine, and energy.

items.title: From Drones to Bomb Hoaxes: Is Europe’s Civil Aviation Facing a New Form of Hybrid Warfare?
items.summary: A wave of false bomb threats has triggered flight diversions, emergency procedures and fighter jet scrambles across Europe, raising questions about a possible new tactic aimed at disrupting civilian aviation. On Nov. 5, 2026, fighters were scrambled by NATO air forces in different parts of Europe to respond to potential threats involving civilian airliners. items.title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
items.summary: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using.

items.title: The New Romantics

items.title: If Fritz Lang’s Iconic Film Metropolis Had a Kraftwerk Soundtrack
items.summary: The case of the copyright history of Fritz Lang’s influential sci-fi masterpiece Metropolis is as convoluted as the history of its film print. Lang’s vision and his original almost-three-hour cut were doomed to censorship right from the start. The Nazis took out its more socialist scenes. It’s been edited, colorized, put back together and restored. Wikipedia currently lists nine different versions. Similarly, ownership of the film shifted from distributors back to the public domain, then out of it again, once more of the original footage was rediscovered.

items.title: Qantas Offloads 44 Old Boeing 737s as Airbus A321XLR and A220 Deliveries Accelerate
items.summary: CANBERRA- Qantas (QF) is moving ahead with a major domestic fleet renewal after agreeing to sell 44 Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft to British aviation aftermarket specialist AerFin. The transaction, announced on November 4, 2026, includes 88 CFM56-7B engines and will allow the Australian airline to progressively retire older aircraft as replacements enter service across its network. The agreement covers aircraft transfers over seven years rather than an immediate withdrawal from operations.

items.title: Why United Airlines' Unusual Boeing 767-400ER Seats With 43 Inches Of Pitch Aren't For Passengers
items.summary: United Airlines operates some of the most unusual economy seats in the industry, and passengers lucky enough to find them can enjoy an experience that rivals premium economy. Hidden toward the back of the carrier's Boeing 767 aircraft are four seats offering an impressive 43 inches of pitch, extendable leg rests, footrests, and additional recline. With an entire foot more pitch than United's standard economy seats, these unusual accommodations are the most spacious options available in the airline's economy cabin.

items.title: Where to Play, Eat, and Stay in Jackson Hole, Wyoming
items.summary: As I scaled the via ferrata at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort, I was focused on the short view, scouting out my next few handholds and footholds. Only when I stopped to rest did I take it all in. Hawks circled overhead and then soared below us, where the Snake River and the valley floor lay under cloud-dappled sunlight. We saw a pika (a small, rabbit-like mammal), spotted a fox, and caught sight of a moose as we made our way back down the mountain. That climb was part of a fall trip to Jackson, Wyoming, which has quickly become one of my favorite national park gateway towns.

items.title: SNC Withdraws From Navy T-45 Replacement Competition
items.summary: Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) has withdrawn from the U.S. Navy’s competition to replace its T-45 Goshawk jet trainer, narrowing the field of companies pursuing the Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) contract. SNC confirmed it did not submit a proposal by the Navy’s Oct. 30 deadline, according to Breaking Defense. The company said it could not responsibly bid under the program’s current contract structure but remains interested in the effort if the Navy revisits its approach. SNC had been pursuing the contract with its Freedom trainer, a clean-sheet design developed specifically for the Navy requirement.

items.title: Volcanic eruptions and less sunlight made Victorian Era kids sicker
items.summary: The Industrial Revolution overturned centuries of English agrarian life, but the rapid societal transformation came at steep costs to the laborers themselves. Miserable working conditions, poor housing, and pollution all contributed to health problems among factory employees as well as their families. Meanwhile, children faced countless diseases like rickets, which prevents developing skeletons from adequately mineralizing. However, a recent investigation into a 19th century Quaker cemetery in northeast England indicates the Industrial Revolution wasn’t the sole culprit behind this rickets endemic.

items.title: Food contains thousands of overlooked chemicals. This physicist is mapping them
items.summary: Computational physicist Giulia Menichetti is looking for “dark matter” in our food. In addition to known macronutrients, vitamins and minerals, the things we eat contain a whole world of natural chemicals we have no idea about. And those chemicals may affect our health. “They have the ability to interact, to bind to human proteins, to modulate our microbiome,” says Menichetti of Harvard Medical School. “We want to leverage this to talk more and more about the role of food and nutrition in human health.”

items.title: Why Boeing 787-9 Operators Are Moving From 2-2-2 To 1-2-1 Business Class
items.summary: When Boeing launched the 787 Dreamliner, airlines celebrated its lightweight composite fuselage, lower cabin altitude, and game-changing fuel efficiency. When looking inside the forward cabin, many operators opted for dense 2-2-2 or 2-3-2 seating configurations. A decade later, those layouts are rapidly being torn out. Across the globe, legacy long-haul carriers are investing hundreds of millions of dollars to refit their 787-9 fleets with modern single-passenger suite designs.

items.title: Air France-KLM beats profit forecasts, but KLM plans 1,000 job cuts
items.summary: Air France-KLM’s adjusted operating profit rose by €126 million ($142 million) year-on-year to €1.35 billion ($1.52 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, the airline group reported on November 5, 2026, as higher ticket revenue and strong cargo demand offset rising fuel costs. Though the result exceeded analysts’ expectations of €1.1 billion ($1.24 billion), the group raised its annual fuel cost forecast again, while its Dutch subsidiary KLM announced a restructuring that will leave it with approximately 1,000 fewer positions over the coming years.
