items.title: The Aircraft Set To Replace The Most Beloved Aircraft In The Sky In 2026
items.summary: As the end of the era of quatjets approaches on the horizon, carriers around the world are still reworking fleet strategies to replace iconic aircraft like Airbus A380. The superjumbo still tops the charts as one of the most popular planes in the sky for its sheer scale as much as the features that a double-decker jetliner makes possible inside the cabin. Yet, with a shuttered assembly line, airlines like Emirates and Qantas must choose from a short list of next-gen twinjets for the successor to Airbus’ flying giant.

items.title: Why one positive E. coli sample put a Pittsburgh-area community under a boil-water advisory
items.summary: A boil-water advisory was issued on Nov. 2, 2026, by officials in Center Township in Beaver County, 25 miles from Pittsburgh, after a routine sample tested positive for coliform bacteria, including E. coli, according to the township’s water authority. The advisory stayed in place while the authority kept testing, and Central Valley School District students stayed out of school buildings and attended class remotely on Nov. 3-4 as a precaution. The authority lifted the advisory on Nov. 4. A single positive sample of E. coli can upend daily routines for an entire community, from what people drink to how they wash dishes, and leave residents wondering how worried they should be.

items.title: Pear Crisp
items.summary: Apples get all the attention when fruit crisp season rolls around, but pear recipes deserve a little time in the spotlight, too. Pears are naturally sweet, delicately floral, and practically melt in your mouth when baked. This easy pear crisp recipe makes the most of them, tucking tender slices beneath a buttery, brown sugar oat topping that turns golden and crunchy in the oven. It’s everything you love about a classic fruit crisp, with a little more elegance and a lot less peeling.

items.title: Retired jet engines finding second life powering AI data centers
items.summary: An old jet engine removed from a Boeing 737 or Airbus A320 can be worth more as a generator for an AI data center than a parts dealer could recover by selling its components. This new reality is helping to spawn an industry built around the premise that there’s money to be made by repurposing retired turbine engines in the data-center era. AI data center developers can wait years for a grid connection, and that’s a problem in an industry that is racing to build out computing infrastructure. Buying retired jet engines and converting them into generators gives developers a way to produce electricity on site and bring their servers online far sooner.

items.title: Review: Qdoba's New Chicken Tinga Is A Welcomed Menu Addition, But It Can't Beat An Upgraded Classic

items.title: An Old Summer Ski School in Iceland’s Highlands Is Now a Hotel Worth the 3.5-Hour Drive From Reykjavík
items.summary: After hours of driving over uneven, rocky terrain, I entered Iceland’s Ásgarður Valley and rolled down my window. A giant rainbow arced over the valley, dwarfing the region’s tallest mountain and ending right at Highland Base Kerlingarfjöll, where I’d stay for the next few nights. The wooden building before me seemed like it had grown out of the valley floor. The property sits on the site of a ski school where generations of Icelanders skied every summer until it closed in 2000 when the snowfields shrank.

items.title: How Human Civilization Began
items.summary: In a recent video, Kurzgesagt explores what we know about the first human civilizations that formed some 12,000 years ago and how they led to the first cities and the invention of writing. What we know about human history is only a fraction of the full story. Much of the rest is like dark matter, invisible to us. We can’t see it, and we can only see the effects of its presence. But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

items.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.summary: We’re introducing StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve. State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed.

items.title: NASA’s Swift telescope has burned up, months after a robot sent to save it failed – here’s why it’s so hard to boost a satellite
items.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory took its last look at the sky on Oct. 20, 2026, while orbiting about 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth. NASA ended the telescope’s mission three days later, because Swift had sunk so low that drag from the thin air there meant its telescopes couldn’t hold steady. The telescope reentered the atmosphere on Nov. 4 above the North Sumatra region of Indonesia and largely burned up, an abrupt ending to two decades spent observing powerful cosmic explosions. Swift’s reentry comes after a failed rescue mission in the summer of 2026.

items.title: Midterms are bad for incumbents – and even worse when energy prices are high
items.summary: As Democrats and Republicans look at the overwhelming results of the 2026 midterm election, it’s worth remembering what has become a political axiom in America: “ It’s the economy, stupid.” Democratic strategist James Carville famously said that to presidential candidate Bill Clinton in 1992, but he might have said “it’s energy prices” instead. The cost of energy underlies much of the economy, making energy and politics inseparable, especially when gasoline prices rise. Midterm elections have historically been difficult for incumbent presidents and often shift the balance of power in Washington, D.C.

items.title: Inkitt Builds a One-Shot PR Creator with Resumable Agent Orchestration
items.summary: Inkitt built a one-shot pull request creator that automates small, low-risk code changes from task intake to draft PR creation. Its event-driven orchestrator persists workflow state, coordinates short-lived coding agent containers, bounds retries, and enforces permission restrictions while retaining human review and approval before changes can be merged. items.title: British police say chopper's phallic flight pattern was unintentional
items.summary: The National Police Air Service in England said a helicopter flight path that appeared to draw male genitalia in the sky was completely unintentional.

items.title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
items.summary: Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. They argue that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences. By Matt Saunders…

items.title: OpenAI says it will protect local resources and report on the impact of its data centers
items.summary: These new pledges come after Americans rebuked the explosion of data centers in local elections this week. OpenAI has pledged to conserve resources and be more transparent, just after Americans had overwhelmingly voted against data centers in the midterms. The company has published a National Community Compact⁠, which details what people can expect from its future data centers. It has also released a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint, which proposes policies to give communities a voice and protect them from new costs if a development is built where they live.

items.title: A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves
items.summary: Scientists have discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle-repair protein into a more powerful version dubbed "Super HGF," more than doubling its ability to bind to a key receptor while protecting it from age-related chemical damage. The breakthrough, supported by early mouse experiments, could eventually help combat muscle loss and preserve strength as people age.

items.title: The Best Airbnbs in Colorado, Including a Ski-In Chalet and a Cliffside Cabin
items.summary: These close-to-nature abodes will get you excited for winter. I’ve always found Colorado a little hard to resist. After a handful of trips, I’ve explored everything from Aspen’s glitzy streets to Denver’s spirited food and cocktail scene to the many smaller towns in between—and somehow, there’s still more to discover. With four national parks; miles of hiking and biking trails; world-class ski resorts; and cities brimming with independent shops, restaurants, and bars, Colorado is a year-round playground with plenty to keep you busy (and plenty of reasons to come back).

items.title: These Are the Most Affordable Ski Resorts in the US for 2026-27
items.summary: Ski trips aren’t exactly known for their budget-friendly prices. From resort fees to slope passes to rental equipment, the costs add up quickly. Many Americans also travel to seek out the best slopes, adding significant transportation costs to the final bill. That being said, there are ski resorts throughout the Rockies, Southwest, Pacific Northwest, and New England that offer valuable deals with enviable slopes. Though vacations aren’t cheap by any means, they won’t take years to pay off—especially not at these affordable ski resorts identified by a recent HomeToGo study.

items.title: Silica, an FPS and RTS hybrid that mixes a smidge of Dune and Helldivers together, has left early access and entered 1.0
items.summary: The concept of fusing an RTS and an FPS always sounds like a fun one, and since 2023 Martin Melichárek has been trying to make a new take on the combination under the watchful eye of DayZ devs Bohemia Interactive through Silica. Today marks the day that Silica leaves early access and enters 1.0, fully fleshing out its hybrid and mish mash of Dune's Arrakis and Helldivers ' Terminids.
